items.title: Nepal flash flood: What triggered the deadly Himalayan disaster?
items.summary: A devastating flash flood has struck Nepal’s Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, leaving at least eight people dead and hundreds reported missing. The disaster swept through the Bhote Koshi River basin, causing widespread destruction to villages, roads, bridges and major hydropower projects. Authorities say hundreds of travellers are unaccounted for, including foreign tourists from several countries. Rescue teams, supported by helicopters and emergency personnel, are continuing search and evacuation operations across the affected region.

items.title: Expired meat, cockroaches found at Bengaluru clubs during food safety inspections
items.summary: Food safety officials found a series of hygiene and storage violations at some of Bengaluru’s prominent private clubs, including expired food, poor kitchen sanitation, improper storage and products that did not carry mandatory label details. The latest inspections covered 10 clubs, including the Bowring Club, Century Club, Karnataka State Cricket Association (KSCA) Club, Race Course Club, Catholic Club, Badminton Club, Tennis Club, Vijayanagara Club, Mahalakshmi Layout Club and Malleshwaram Club. At the KSCA Club, which operates a canteen at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium, inspectors found expired fish and other food products being stored on the premises. A stock of toor dal did not have details such as the packing date, batch number and maximum retail price. The inspection also flagged hygiene and food-handling practices at the club. Officials found that food handlers were not maintaining adequate personal hygiene and that vegetarian and non-vegetarian food was not being stored separately. Tilapia fish was also found without the required label details. The kitchen had plastic cutting boards, while the drainage system was blocked and the frozen-storage area was found to be unhygienic. items.title: CJI Surya Kant says Collegium examining allegations by Justice Sandeep Mehta against Rajasthan acting CJ
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Wednesday said that he has taken note of concerns raised by Supreme Court Justice Sandeep Mehta regarding Rajasthan High Court Acting Chief Justice SP Sharma. In a press statement issued on Wednesday evening, the CJI said that allegations against a sitting judge has to go through the established institutional process and a decision can be taken only after giving Justice Sharma an opportunity to respond to the allegations. The press statement was issued by the CJI after Bar & Bench reported on three letters written by Justice Mehta to the CJI seeking the transfer of Justice Sharma from Rajasthan over allegations including manipulation of case listings and misuse of office. Justice Mehta’s letters urged the Collegium to appoint a Chief Justice from another High Court to head the Rajasthan High Court with immediate effect. Justice Mehta accused Justice Sharma of manipulating case listings in favour of rich litigants and misusing his administrative powers ahead of his retirement, due later next month. In his August 2 letter, Justice Mehta referred to complaints allegedly made by judges of the Rajasthan High Court about Justice Sharma’s conduct

items.title: Akash’s Dalit identity known to cops who tortured and killed him, finds CB-CID
items.summary: The CB-CID chargesheet in the custodial death of 26-year-old Dalit youth Akash Delison says the six policemen accused in his death knew that he belonged to the Scheduled Caste (SC) Devendrakula Vellalar community and assaulted him with the intention of causing his death. All six have been charged with offences under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, along with provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Akash, from Sivaganga district, died on March 8 while under treatment at the Government Rajaji Hospital (GRH) in Madurai, two days after his arrest by the Manamadurai police. Police had arrested Akash and another man, Guna, on March 6, in connection with an attempted murder case. Even though the chargesheet on Akash’s custodial torture and murder was filed before the III Additional District Judge for Protection of Civil Rights (PCR) cases in Madurai on June 18, Akash’s parents received a copy only recently. It names Inspector Dileepan, Sub-Inspector K Guhan, Grade-I Constable S Kaleeswaran, driver constable P Mahendran, constable L Deivendran, and constable B Palaniyappan as accused.
